newsitem.title: UK: Poland seen seeking regional markets to sell sugar.
newsitem.headline: Poland seen seeking regional markets to sell sugar.

text.p: Poland is likely to seek out neighbouring markets during 1997 to sell its expected increased production, Czarnikow Sugar said in a report on Thursday. It cited local estimates saying Polish sugar output would reach 2.1 million tonnes in white value terms.
Czarnikow pegged its raw value estimate for Polish 1996/97 production just below this at 2.20 million tonnes, after a previous 1.72 million. Its initial estimate in August was 2.05.

"We have not altered our consumption figure for next year at 1.70 million tonnes (raw value) and there will clearly be a larger quantity seeking export outlets, mainly in neighbouring markets, over the course of next year," Czarnikow said.

Poland's 1996/97 sugar surplus could be as much as 500,000 tonnes, despite a announcement from the government that it would buy an undisclosed amount for state reserves, in addition to an agreement to subsidise 118,000 tonnes of exports.

It added that the driving strength behind the improved Polish crop had been a significant 19 percent expansion in beet area to 450,000 hectares and noted that potential yields had also continued to improve.
